description: We are Team Afaq working on Flame in Freefall for NASA Space Apps 2026. We are building an AI dashboard that analyzes NASA microgravity fire safety data (BASS, SAFFIRE) to assist spacecraft engineers. Looking for team members skilled in AI/Data Science, Full-Stack Dev, or UI/UX.
summary:
FLAREX is a scientific intelligence platform designed to make NASA's curated microgravity combustion research data easier to explore, understand, and analyze. The platform brings together experimental datasets, measurements, and scientific documentation through a unified interface, allowing researchers to investigate experiments, explore data, and trace information back to its original sources.

FLAREX uses a structured data pipeline, quality checks, provenance tracking, and comparability rules to help users interpret scientific evidence responsibly. Its AI assistant combines BM25 and hashed TF-IDF retrieval with deterministic tools to retrieve relevant information and provide source-grounded responses.

By addressing the challenges of fragmented research data, inconsistent formats, and difficult source tracing, FLAREX aims to make scientific exploration more accessible, transparent, and reliable while preserving the limitations and context of the original experiments.
details:
FLAREX (Microgravity Combustion Intelligence) is a scientific intelligence platform designed to make microgravity combustion research data more accessible, organized, and understandable. It focuses on curated experiments from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database.

The platform provides a unified environment where researchers can explore combustion investigations, browse datasets and measurements, examine experimental conditions, and trace scientific information back to its original sources. Its data pipeline transforms curated research files into structured Parquet tables, which are queried through DuckDB and served through a FastAPI backend to a modern Next.js web interface.

One of FLAREX’s key features is its AI assistant, which uses BM25 and hashed TF-IDF hybrid lexical retrieval alongside 22 deterministic tools to help users find relevant scientific information. Responses are designed around source traceability and scientific evidence rather than unsupported assumptions.

The project offers several benefits: it reduces the effort required to navigate fragmented research materials, improves access to experimental data, makes data limitations more visible, and helps researchers understand whether measurements can be meaningfully compared. Its quality and provenance features preserve important distinctions between measured, computed, raw, and derived values.

FLAREX’s intended impact is to support more transparent and efficient scientific exploration of combustion behavior in microgravity. By organizing existing research evidence and making its context easier to understand, the platform can help researchers spend less time searching through scattered files and more time investigating scientific questions.

The project was developed using Python, FastAPI, DuckDB, Parquet, and SQL on the backend, with TypeScript, React, and Next.js on the frontend. It also uses data-processing and retrieval techniques, automated testing, and modern web development tools. No specialized experimental hardware was required for the current software platform.

What makes FLAREX creative is its evidence-first approach: it does not simply display datasets or generate answers. It connects scientific measurements to their experimental context, source files, quality information, and comparability rules. The team also prioritized scientific integrity, data provenance, explicit units, missing-data handling, and clear disclosure of limitations. The platform does not invent measurements, silently modify scientific values, or claim that unrelated experiments are directly comparable.

FLAREX aims to turn scattered scientific data into organized, traceable, and useful knowledge while keeping scientific accuracy and transparency at the center of the experience.
